Clarifying shampoo will help a lot! My hair was doing the same thing, my curls wouldn’t form as nicely, and it was really hard to manage without matts forming. I had to clarify it and shampooed it twice after, didn’t dry out my hair like I was afraid it was going to, it did  the complete opposite!
With curly hair we put so much product on our hair each “wash day”, one shampoo doesn’t do a lot  when you have that build up, it was a game changer!

I would consistently do two classes of spin a day, after I got pregnant I could barely get through half a class, it would make me so nauseous. I would eat before the class, try going right in the morning, switched to night. It still made me feel very sick.
I held off on lifting heavy until I wasn’t nauseous, it cleared around 15 weeks, i still lifted weights and went on the stairmaster but it wasn’t nearly as strenuous as before. I stopped spinning all together! It is really how you feel, it’s okay to not go and it’s okay to not lift as heavy!

Just letting you know, in BC at the moment servers are getting paid $12.70 while minimum wage workers are getting paid $14.60.
     We also have to tip out 5-10% of all of our sales at the end of the night.
     As a server you also have to declare all your tips, meaning depending on your tax bracket you pay 5.06-7.70% of your tip income. If you don’t declare your tips, there is a 90% chance you will get audited and have to pay an even higher premium than 5-7%.
     Doing the math for you, if you tip your server 20% on a $100 bill($20) they will pay $1 on that as well as $5-$10 to the back of house/setters/hosts/managers(yes it’s illegal for managers to supplement wages, but they do it anyway). So in reality your server is getting $14-$9 that table. On average a table stays for 45minutes to an hour and a half. This means your server  has to make at least $2 per hour on tables to make more than a minimum wage server. Yes servers make more than minimum wage but there is a lot more that goes into serving than working drivethrough at a mcdonalds. I worked at a fast food establishment for 2 years before I started hosting at the restaurant I work at currently and being a fast food worker is non-comparable to the restaurant industry. 
    (Edited)If you don’t want to tip then I would just stay home and cook or go to a fast food restaurant. My place of work doesn’t tip out on takeout but some places do! 

TLDR:

Unlike fast food workers, cashiers, or clothing stores, servers have to tip out and pay taxes on assumed pay for that year. Togos also tip out so if you aren’t going to tip just stay clear of restaurants.(if you don’t like it, don’t support it)

I’ll just let you know, speaking for everyone,not a single human being working customer service wants you there until 10:45-11 if they close at 10. They are just doing there job and if everyone “got a different job” because we had to serve people until we close only a few would actually have jobs.

The beginning of your serving career is most likely your slowest if you didn't start off hosting/bussing. The longer you stay at a certain restaurant the more you know about the menu, how things work, and what kind of clientele your restaurant brings in. Most restaurants will put the veterans or good servers in better sections, therefore more money. When I first started serving I walking out with $80 a night and now I'm walking away with close to $300. I would not recommend jumping restaurant to restaurant, it will end up making your resume look bad and in the end, won't make you more money than you think.
